rows.not_applicable_reason: Email open tracking requires a tracking pixel. We do not use one: it is a privacy intrusion, it is blocked by most clients, and a blocked pixel is indistinguishable from an unopened email — so the signal would be unreliable as well as invasive.
Same reason as device_delivered: we declined to build open-pixel tracking (§8.2).
No mobile carrier exposes SMS read receipts to the sender. This tier cannot be measured for SMS by anyone, including us.
A voice call has no "opened" concept. Answering the call is the delivery, and the keypad press is the acknowledgement.
A siren or public-address broadcast produces no digital receipt of any kind. Confirmation requires a human — see the field relay channel.
A physical broadcast has no "opened" concept at all.
A siren cannot receive an acknowledgement; only a human relay or a citizen who later opens the PWA can confirm anything about a siren-only delivery.
A physical, door-to-door broadcast has no "opened" event.
The relay operator's keypad confirmation is a human attestation, recorded separately from digital delivery (Rule 9) — see relay_confirmation, not delivery_event.
A peer-to-peer transfer never touches our server, so there is no provider to accept it.
